title: A cross fade plays smoothly in the editor, the way it looks in the export
goal: Playing a video in the editor, a cross fade between two clips flickers on and off, while the exported file shows the same fade cleanly. Playback in the editor has to show every frame of a transition the way export does, with no frame where one side or the whole picture drops out.
notes:
User, 2026-11-20: "i see a weird bug where on a video transition on i think a cross fade, playing it back in the editor mode had it flickering off and on. but cutting the exported video it was fine, i think there's a rendering bug." They were not sure it was a cross fade; check other transitions (push, 3D) too if the dissolve does not reproduce. I could not see their document (no document open over MCP), and did not reproduce it.

Why export and playback differ: export renders every frame and waits for both shots; live playback reads frames ahead through the play pass and frame queue (Sources/PhotonzCore/MoviePlayPass.swift, Sources/PhotonzCore/MovieFrameQueue.swift), which during a dissolve must hold frames for TWO places at once (MoviePlayPass.swift:28-31, 246, 337-340; MovieFrameQueue.swift:79-90, which already records 'a dissolve stuck that way, 2026-10-07').

Suspect, not confirmed: when one side's frame is not decoded in time, the compositor draws that layer missing for a frame (on and off), rather than holding its last frame. Recent commits touching exactly this budget, worth bisecting: ad24392f4 (fast passes skip frames nothing depends on), cf12e8b00 and b9cf61d13 (hunt and frame budget, Next), c771adfbb (long edit plays). The fix must not be 'wait for the frame' if that drops playback frames; holding the newest decoded frame of the late side is the likely shape, plus fixing why it is late.

Overlaps: a-long-edit-with-transitions-plays-scrubs-and-ed (p1, seq 10) is about speed on long edits with transitions; this one is about correctness of what is drawn. Keep them separate but say in both logs if one fix serves both. The rotating check's an-editing-session-walk fails on blank frames during play; say why it did not catch this (a dissolve may not be in it, or it checks only fully blank frames).
acceptance: Reproduced first, in the probe at Next defaults: a two-clip edit with a cross fade (dissolve) between two different recordings, and a second case with a dissolve between two parts of the SAME recording, played at 1x through the transition. Capture every displayed frame during playback (the frames the player actually puts on screen, not an offscreen render) and name in the audit which frames go wrong and how (blank, only the outgoing shot, only the incoming shot, a stale frame).
Find the cause before fixing and write it in the audit, with the evidence. Do not assume the suspect in the notes.

Measured bar: for each displayed frame in the transition, compare it to the export's frame at the same time; every frame is within a small stated tolerance (mean pixel difference measured and listed), and the mean luminance across the transition never jumps by more than the fade itself would cause between neighbouring frames. Today's build fails this on the reproduction.
Also passes at 0.5x and 2x, after a scrub that lands just before the transition, and with the transition starting the moment play is pressed.
A walk or unit test keeps it fixed: it fails on today's code and passes after.

A reel under queue/audits/ (editor playback capture beside the export, before and after) named in the audit. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: Reproduced (probe, Next defaults) with a new step expectTransitionPlaysAsExported: every picture the canvas is handed while a transition plays vs the export's picture of the same moment (streamed like an MP4), plus which frame each side was drawn from. On the fixture and on two of the user's HEVC 3456x2234 screen recordings (VFR, key frames ~2.2s apart), playing from rest at 1x, from the first frame, 0.5x and 2x matched the export (mean diff ~2/255, every frame exact), even with 14 of 16 cores busy, and filmed on screen (filmWindow) the fade was smooth. What failed every time: Space right after a scrub landing just before the dissolve, both sides drawn from frames up to 34 behind (rec-a frame 146 for 180: a second old, a screenshot thumbnail popping in the corner).

Cause (timing logs in MovieSweeper): (1) a pass opened mid-GOP takes 614ms for its first frame; MoviePlayPass.serves called it fallen behind after 4 frames and restarted it at the playhead, which decodes from the SAME key frame, so passes 176,181,186,191 opened and none read a frame. (2) MovieFramesInHand stood in for a late frame borrowed past a clip's stretch with a frame from back inside the stretch (within: playedSourceFrames excludes transition handles), so a late borrowed frame jumped the shot back up to a second, then forward again: the on/off flicker, absent in export which never stands in. Fixed both; unit tests fail on old code (borrowed stand-in 60 for 64 and 41 for 37; serves with key frames).

Left open (why this stays pending): after a scrub landing ~1s past a key frame and an immediate Space (or 0.4s later), the outgoing side still holds a frame (175 for 178..193, a tenth of a second old instead of a second) for ~0.6s while the first frame decodes; play start cancels the resting read that was already decoding there (stopSweeps in fetch when playing). Next step: play waits for the first frame under the playhead (Premiere does), or the play pass adopts the resting read. The committed walk has no scrub case because it would be red; the fixture lands near a key frame so it passes there anyway. Evidence on the user's recordings kept out of the public repo: ~/Library/Caches/Photonz Cross Fade Evidence.

Why an-editing-session-walk did not catch it: expectPlaybackNeverBlank looks 30 times over 21s, fails only on a clip area >90% see-through, counts only a dissolve inside one clip (incomingMovieFrameSourceMS, not edit-point transitions), and plays from rest, where the dissolve is exact on this Mac.

Two causes fixed and committed (5b1effa70): borrowed transition frames stand in from the borrowed stretch; no restart of a play pass onto the same key frame. Walk a-cross-fade-plays-as-exported-walk passes at Next defaults (1x, first frame, 0.5x, 2x; jump-cut and two-clip dissolves). Still open: the after-a-scrub item, Space right after a scrub ~1s past a key frame holds a slightly old frame for ~0.6s. Audit: queue/audits/2026-11-20-a-cross-fade-plays-smoothly-in-the-editor-the-wa.json

Reproduced the open item on today's build (user's rec-a/rec-b, scrub landing 0.2s before the dissolve, Space 0.4s later): 14 of 24 looks stale, rec-a frame 175 for 179/180, then the borrowed side 181 for 183..191; the pass sat at 177 for ~0.45s decoding from the key frame. Did NOT reproduce on the repo fixture (3.6s), on a synthetic 10s 3456x2234 HEVC with 2.2s GOPs, or on the reference footage: all decode fast enough.

Chose: at sound speeds, play from rest waits until the frame under the playhead and the next 3 are in hand (max 0.8s; MoviePlayPass.startsWithFramesAhead / soundStartWaitMS, PhotonzDocument.readyToStartPlaying), and the sound starts with the clock (preRollWithSound; documentClockWaiting gates startAudio), over adopting the resting read into the play pass, because the resting read is rough-sized and cannot become a sharp pass, and waiting is what Premiere does. Not applied to a speed change or a scrub mid-play.

After: user's recording, 3 runs at 1x after a scrub plus 0.5x, 2x, from the first frame, from rest: every picture drawn from its own frame, mean diff 2.0, worst 2.7. Space waits 416ms after a scrub, 45ms from rest (41-60ms on the fixture). 15 playback walks pass (sound, speed, never-blinks, editing session). Full Scripts/test.sh green. Unit test readyToStartWithSound.
left rough: the committed walk's after-a-scrub cases pass on old code too (the fixture decodes too fast); only the unit test fails on old code. A slow-decoding public fixture did not earn a task.

All three causes fixed (5b1effa70, f599c5fdc): borrowed frames stand in from the borrowed stretch; no restart onto the same key frame; Space from rest at sound speeds waits for the frame under the playhead and the next 3 (max 0.8s) with the sound starting with the clock. Verified on the user's recording after a scrub at 1x (3 runs), 0.5x, 2x, from the first frame and from rest: every picture matches the export (mean 2.0/255, worst 2.7). Space waits 416ms after a scrub, 45ms from rest. Walk a-cross-fade-plays-as-exported-walk + 14 playback walks pass at Next defaults; unit test readyToStartWithSound; full test.sh green. Audit updated.
